Q: How to retrieve argv and argc in assembly language for x86_64 processors on Linux (SYSTEM V) OS A:

The argc/argv are pushed by OS on stack, so your assembly code needs to pop them out from stack into registers in order to use them. There's a tutorial about it with detailed diagram of stack layout as well as demo code to show the command line arguments using just assembly code. See the document/tutorial from this GitHub repo:

https://github.com/LilSuperUser/x86_64-asm-tutorials/blob/main/notes/013-CLI_arguments.md

Note that the example assembly code shown in the tutorial is written in nasm format/flavor. In order to use it, you will need to install "nasm". On Debian distro (or all those derived from Debian), you can install it with this command:

sudo apt install nasm

To generate the executable:

nasm -f elf64 sample.s -o sample.o
ld sample.o -o sample

For other distros, the install command would be different but you probably knew how already. If your assembler is not "nasm", you should translate it to the proper syntax, but it shouldn't be hard.

The improved example code.

Stack Overflow encourages showing actual code embedded inside the question/answer instead of external link because the content referenced by external link might disappear someday. The original demo code is from LilSuperUser but it contains a bug that when the argc is greater than a digit can hold, the output would be gibberish. A revised version is thus shown below. Thanks to Peter Cordes's suggestion to fix the bug.

%macro printDigit 1                            ; defining a macro to print a digit passed to it
    mov rax, %1                                ; load the passed digit into rax
    add rax, 48                                ; convert the digit to its ASCII value by adding 48
    mov [digit], rax                           ; write value of rax into the reserved 8 bytes of 'digit'
    mov rax, 1                                 ; prepare for sys_write (system call)
    mov rdi, 1                                 ; file descriptor for stdout
    mov rsi, digit                             ; load pointer to 'digit' variable
    mov rdx, 8                                 ; load number of bytes to write (starting from pointer) into rdx
    syscall                                    ; invoke the syscall
%endmacro                                      ; end the macro definition

%macro printNline 0                            ; defining a macro to print a newline character
    mov rax, 1                                 ; load 1 into rax (syscall number for sys_write)
    mov rdi, 1                                 ; load 1 into rdi (file descriptor for stdout)
    mov rsi, nline                             ; load pointer to 'nline' character into rsi
    mov rdx, 1                                 ; load 1 (number of bytes to write) into rdx
    syscall                                    ; invoke the syscall
%endmacro                                      ; end the macro definition

%macro printString 1                           ; defining a macro to print a string (pointer to string is passed)
    mov rsi, %1                                ; load the pointer to string into rsi
    xor rcx, rcx                               ; clear rcx to count the length of the string
    %%getLenLoop:                              ; loop to calculate the length of the string
        mov al, [rsi + rcx]                    ; move value pointed by rsi + rcx into lower byte of rax (al)
        test al, al                            ; perform a bitwise AND between al and al, result zero iff al = 0
        jz %%done                              ; if result of test = 0, jump to %%done label
        inc rcx                                ; increment rcx if al is not 0
        jmp %%getLenLoop                       ; jump to %%getLenLoop to execute a loop
    %%done:                                    ; definition of %%done label, executed when al = 0
        mov rax, 1                             ; load 1 into rax (sys_write)
        mov rdi, 1                             ; load 1 into rdi (stdout)
        mov rsi, %1                            ; load pointer to string into rsi
        mov rdx, rcx                           ; load number of bytes to write (length) into rdx
        syscall                                ; invoke the syscall
%endmacro                                      ; end the macro definition

%macro exit 0                                  ; macro to exit the program
    mov rax, 60                                ; load 60 into rax (sys_exit)
    xor rdi, rdi                               ; load 0 into rdi (exit code)
    syscall                                    ; invoke the syscall
%endmacro                                      ; end the macro definition

section .data
    argc_str db 'Number of arguments are: ', 0 ; string literal for displaying the argument count
    argn_str db 'Argument number ', 0          ; string literal for displaying each argument number
    ending db ' is: ', 0                       ; string literal for formatting output

    nline db 10                                ; label to one B which holds the newline character's ASCII value

section .bss
    align 8
    digit resb 8                               ; reserving 8 bytes under name 'digit' for digit storage
    argc resb 8                                ; reserving 8 bytes under name 'argc' for argument count

section .text
    global _start

_start:
    pop rax                                    ; pop the stack into rax (rax holds argc from stack) and increment rsp
    mov [argc], rax                            ; write the value of rax into 'argc' (pointer to argc in memory)
    printString argc_str                       ; call the macro with the pointer to string (argc_str)
    mov rdi, [argc]                            ; call printNumber to print argc
    call printNumber
    printNline                                 ; call the macro to print the newline character

printArgs:                                     ; label used to print the arguments in the stack
    xor rbx, rbx                               ; clear rbx to use it as a counter
    printArgsLoop:                             ; start of the loop
        cmp rbx, [argc]                        ; compare the value of rbx with the value in 'argc'
        jge printArgsDone                      ; if rbx >= value in 'argc', jump to label printArgsDone
        inc rbx                                ; if rbx < *argc, increment rbx by 1
        printString argn_str                   ; call macro with pointer to string (argn_str) to print it
        mov rdi, rbx                           ; call printNumber on current counter
        call printNumber
        printString ending                     ; call the macro with pointer to string (ending) to print it
        pop r15                                ; pop the stack into r15 (r15 has the pointer to the first argument, i.e., path)
        printString r15                        ; call the macro to print the first argument string
        printNline                             ; print the newline character
        jmp printArgsLoop                      ; jump back to printArgsLoop to execute a loop
    printArgsDone:                             ; executes if rbx >= value in 'argc'
        exit                                   ; call the exit macro to exit the program

; Recursively print higher digits first
; Input: rdi
printNumber:
    cmp rdi, 10
    jl .print1Digit

    mov rax, rdi
    xor rdx, rdx
    mov rcx, 10
    div rcx              ; rax = quotient, rdx = remainder
    push rdx             ; save remainder
    mov rdi, rax
    call printNumber     ; recursive call with quotient
    pop rax              ; restore remainder
    printDigit rax       ; print lowest digit
    ret

.print1Digit:
    printDigit rdi       ; print single digit
    ret

Q: How do you squash commits into one patch with git format-patch? A:

An alternative without temporary branches

bash -c '
commit1=xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
commit2=yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy

# take log information from commit2
git log --pretty=email ${commit2}^...${commit2}

# mark log information end like git format-patch
echo ---

# add diff stat and summary like git format-patch
git diff ${commit1}..${commit2} | git apply --stat --summary

# mark diff stat and summary end like git format-patch
echo

# generate diff from ${commit1} to ${commit2}
git diff ${commit1}..${commit2}

# mark diff end like git format-patch
echo --

# add git version like git format-patch
git -v | sed "s/git version //"

# add a trailing line like git format-patch
echo
' > 001-from-x-to-y.patch

Q: How can I create pseudo-random numbers depending on multiple integer parameters? A:

2026 update: It appears that the C++ standard has always specified the behavior of std::seed_seq::generate() such that the same input values will always result in the same output, even when compiled with a different compiler/standard library. That said, the algorithm seems designed to work with the MT19937 PRNG (e.g. doing something different when n=>623) so I'd (personally) be inclined to use something else.

The cryptographic approach suggested [by Maarten] would would be to use something like a HKDF, where you use a cryptographic hash (like SHA256) to extract the entropy (i.e. "randomness") from your input values in a deterministic manner (e.g. taking care of endianness) and then use another cryptographic primitive to "stretch" this entropy out to produce your random output. If you're not familiar with the cryptographic world these things can be awkward as there's a lot of terminology.

As a minor point, I'd suggest against using the MT19937 PRNG as it's relatively expensive to seed and it sounds like you'd be doing this a lot. There are other algorithms that are much cheaper, I personally like Sebastiano's xoshiro256 family or you could use Melissa's PCG family. Melissa O'Neill's site is a very useful resource if you're new to PRNGs.

That said, if you're going the HKDF route you may as well just use the "expansion" step as a PRNG as it will directly produce uniform values. These can be transformed into bounded/uniform values easily: Melissa has a good review for ints here, or Vigna describes a conventional transform for binary IEEE-754 floats at the bottom of here (so is valid for float and double on most common CPUs).

2023 update: The MT19937 would seem to be difficult to predict given its enormous state space, but in fact it's been shown almost trivial. For example, searching for "predicting mt19937" leads to https://github.com/kmyk/mersenne-twister-predictor which will give you the state of the RNG from 624 consecutive 32bit integer draws. Using a CSPRNG would protect you from this, and is what using the output of a HKDF would give you. PCG makes this more difficult than the Mersenne Twister, but given that it's optimised for speed can't expend too much work doing this.

This answer previously started with, keeping for historical context:

To explain Maarten's issues with std::seed_seq (and to make sure I understand things correctly!) I'll attempt an answer.

The main issue I'd have with potentially suggesting using it (and it sounds like Maarten has the same one) is that the algorithm used by std::seed_seq isn't defined by the standard. Hence it's possible for other standard libraries (e.g. if you use a different compiler or even a different version of the same compiler) to change the implementation and you'd get different values back from the same inputs. Depending on your use case this lack of stability may, or may not, matter. That's a domain specific issue you'd have to decide on as you haven't specified it.

Q: How to perform a rebase without touching any worktree (or tree/blob object)? A:

lowchess already answered the question, but for reference here is the script I ended up using:

echo $(git rev-parse "master~11") > .git/HEAD &&
for COMMIT in $(git rev-list master ^@ --reverse);
do
    echo $(
        echo "$(git log -1 --format="%B" ${COMMIT})" | \
        GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=$(git log -1 --format='%an' ${COMMIT}) \
        GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=$(git log -1 --format='%ae' ${COMMIT}) \
        GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=$(git log -1 --format='%ad' ${COMMIT}) \
        GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=$(git log -1 --format='%cn' ${COMMIT}) \
        GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=$(git log -1 --format='%ce' ${COMMIT}) \
        GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=${GIT_AUTHOR_DATE} \
        git commit-tree -p $(cat .git/HEAD)  $(git rev-parse "${COMMIT}^{tree}") \
    ) > .git/HEAD;
done

This reproduces a git rebase master~11 master --committer-date-is-author-date.

Note1: It is necessary to write echo $(...) > .git/HEAD instead of just ... > .git/HEAD, because otherwise the file is already truncated at the time of parameter execution, which results in git claiming there not to be a repository.

Note2: Don't use git show -s, but git log -1, because the former still tries to compute a diff, even if it should not show it.

Note3: Don't use git push . @:master -f, but git update-ref refs/head/master HEAD.

Q: Why does my Stoat.py code run without issues but the bot doesn't go online/respond to commands? A:

There is at least one definite bug in the posted code: ChaosBot.__init__() throws away every argument passed to it.

You instantiate it with:

bot = ChaosBot(
    case_insensitive=True,
    description="...",
    self_bot=True,
    strip_after_prefix=True,
    token=bot_token,
    owner_ids=[...],
)

but then your subclass does:

class ChaosBot(commands.Bot):
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            command_prefix="/",
        )

Neither args nor kwargs is forwarded. Therefore token, self_bot, owner_ids, case_insensitive, description, etc. never reach commands.Bot. Stoat.py's Bot constructor explicitly accepts these options and ultimately forwards the remaining options to Client.

At minimum, change it to:

class ChaosBot(commands.Bot):
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            *args,
            command_prefix="/",
            **kwargs,
        )

        self.client = None
        self.loop = None

Or, if command_prefix may also be supplied by the caller:

class ChaosBot(commands.Bot):
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
        kwargs.setdefault("command_prefix", "/")
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

        self.client = None
        self.loop = None

There is a second thing worth checking. Stoat.py calls setup_hook() before it opens the WebSocket connection. Your override does quite a bit of work there, including loading every extension:

for filename in listdir("./gears"):
    ...
    await self.load_extension(...)

If one of those extension setup functions never returns, your process will remain running but the bot will never connect. That matches the "program runs indefinitely but bot never goes online" symptom.

Temporarily reduce setup_hook() to:

async def setup_hook(self):
    await super().setup_hook()
    print("setup_hook finished")

and run again. If the bot connects, add the extension loading back one at a time.

Also note that passing the token again here:

bot.run(token=bot_token)

does set the HTTP/WebSocket credentials, so the discarded constructor token alone does not necessarily explain why it never connects. The ignored constructor arguments are still a bug that should be fixed, while a hang inside setup_hook() is the first place I would look for the connection symptom shown here.

Q: Import Python Module into Sublime Text 3 A:

I too had same problem. Couldn't import requests, pandas and some of other modules in sublime. I went to command prompt 'cmd', and first checked python version. If it shows you the version, that means python was installed correctly. Then i ran the command 'pip install requests'. This installed the requests module, and so i installed other ones as well. It's working fine since then on sublime.

Q: How to export csv file with SQL Developer with Pipe separator A:

You can remove string enclosures in SQL Developer. There is a bug though. First overcome the bug: 1) Run a small statement like "select 1 abc from dual" (Ctrl+Enter). 2) Export it (right click on the results set) as delimited setting enclosures to "none" and separator to the charater of your choice.

Now type your query, starting with "set sqlformat delimited" (probably you want ot use spool as well) and run it as a script (F5).

It works :)

Hadrian
